title: Competent embryos take over mixed populations given enough competency or numbers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Competent embryos take over mixed populations given enough competency or numbers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In mixed populations of the 1D artificial embryogeny model, competent embryos starting as a minority came to dominate hardwired ones within two or three generations, and the competency needed to dominate fell as their initial share rose (75 at 10%, 40 at 20%, 10 at 30%), while at 2.5% they did not dominate even at competency 95.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.3. Competent Individuals Take over Mixed Populations

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As their initial proportion in the population increased, competent embryos required progressively less competency to dominate over their hardwired competitors.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “3. Results › 3.3. Competent Individuals Take over Mixed Populations”. Scope: In silico mixed populations of 200 hardwired and competent 1D embryos

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This finite simulation table is highly operational and easy to reproduce from the published specification. Alternative outcomes directly refute the reported thresholds.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Initialize mixed populations at the stated competent fractions and competency levels, then record composition by generation over repeated seeds. The exact dominance thresholds and the 2.5% exception provide direct checks.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stochastic thresholds require enough replicate runs.

The result is parameter-specific.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Takeover is a head-count in a fully specified genetic algorithm, and the mixed-population script is public. A few fraction-by-competency cells may need to be set from the paper rather than the default JSON, which is still reimplementation of a stated model. The numerical thresholds can be confirmed or refuted by those runs.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rerun mixed populations of 200 embryos at the stated initial competent fractions, including 2.5, 10, 20 and 30 percent, across competency levels, and record whether competent genomes exceed half the population within two or three generations. Dominance thresholds near 75, 40 and 10, and failure at 2.5 percent even at competency 95, would confirm the claim; dominance at 2.5 percent or failure at the higher shares would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: The default hyperparameter file does not list every fraction in the claim, so some grid points must be set from the paper.

fields.label: Dimension scores

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In a re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) mixed-population experiment (200 embryos, hardwired plus a competent minority, selection of the top 10% on phenotypic fitness, 20 generations), the competency needed for competent embryos to dominate falls as their initial share rises (about 75 at 10%, 40 at 20%, 10 at 30%), they do not dominate at 2.5% even at competency 95, and when they dominate they do so within two or three generations.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered design: initial competent shares 2.5%, 10%, 20%, 30% (5, 20, 40, 60 of 200) x competency 5, 10, ..., 95 (19 levels) x 50 repeats x 20 generations (generation 1 = initial population, counts taken before selection). 'Dominates' = mean over repeats of the competent share at generation 20 > 0.5. c*(p) = smallest tested competency from which dominance holds at that and every higher tested level (c* = 100 if none). Pass if all of: (P1) c*(10%) > c*(20%) > c*(30%); (P2) |c*(10%) - 75| <= 20, |c*(20%) - 40| <= 20, c*(30%) <= 20; (P3) at 2.5% and competency 95 the mean competent share at generation 20 is <= 0.6; (P4) in every dominating condition at 10/20/30% with competency >= c*, the mean competent share first exceeds 0.5 within 3 rounds of selection (by generation 4).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: refutes if c*(30%) >= c*(10%) (threshold does not fall with share), or |c* - claimed| > 40 for any of 10/20/30%, or at 2.5% competency 95 the mean competent share at generation 20 is > 0.75. Any other failure of P1-P4 -> mixed. A sensitivity run reproducing two quirks of the authors' code (the type label can be overwritten by point mutation and the last structural gene is never mutated) is reported but does not enter the verdict.
